subject: Polity
description: Election, powers, oath, impeachment, VP role

questions.stem: The President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of:

options.option_text: All MPs and all MLAs including nominated ones

questions.explanation: Art 54 — electoral college comprises elected members of Parliament (both Houses) + elected members of state Legislative Assemblies + elected members of the Delhi and Puducherry Assemblies (added by 70th Amendment, 1992). Nominated members and MLCs of state Councils do NOT vote. The votes are weighted (single transferable vote, proportional representation).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The term of office of the President of India is:
questions.explanation: Art 56 — the President holds office for 5 years from the date of taking office. Re-election is allowed without a limit on number of terms — only Dr Rajendra Prasad has served two full terms (1952-62). The President takes oath before the Chief Justice of India (Art 60). Salary (as of recent revisions) is ₹5 lakh per month.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The minimum age required to contest the election for the office of President of India is:
questions.explanation: Art 58 — President: citizen of India, 35+ years, qualified to be a Lok Sabha member, should not hold any office of profit. Same age bar applies to VP and Governors. Lok Sabha / Vidhan Sabha candidates — 25 years; Rajya Sabha / Vidhan Parishad — 30 years. Voting age — 18 years.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The President of India can be removed from office through the process of:

options.option_text: Impeachment for violation of the Constitution

questions.explanation: Art 61 — the President can only be removed by impeachment on the ground of 'violation of the Constitution'. Charges may be initiated in either House, signed by at least one-fourth of the members; after investigation, the other House must pass a resolution with a two-thirds majority of its total membership. No President has been impeached. No-confidence motions target only the Council of Ministers / PM (in Lok Sabha).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Vice-President of India also serves as the:

options.option_text: Ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: Art 64 — the VP is ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. He presides over the Upper House but is NOT a member of it and does not vote in ordinary proceedings (only a casting vote on a tie). The VP acts as President when the office falls vacant (Art 65). Elected by an electoral college of both Houses of Parliament (elected + nominated) by single transferable vote — unlike the President.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, the 11th President of India, came from which professional background?
questions.explanation: Dr Kalam (President 2002-07) was a scientist with India's space programme (ISRO, SLV-3) and defence research (DRDO, integrated missile programme — Agni, Prithvi). He was called the 'Missile Man of India' and was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1997. He is the only scientist to have been President. Other Presidents from unusual backgrounds: Dr S. Radhakrishnan (philosopher, 1962-67), Giani Zail Singh (farmer politician, 1982-87).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The first woman President of India was:
questions.explanation: Pratibha Devisingh Patil served as the 12th President of India (2007-12) and was the first woman to hold the office. Droupadi Murmu (2022- ) is the 15th President and the first from a tribal community. Indira Gandhi was a four-time Prime Minister, not President. Sushma Swaraj served as External Affairs Minister and was Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.
